propositions.text: At most one client holds a given resource at any time (mutual exclusion per resource).
Every lease is time-bounded and expires on its own without the holder's cooperation, so a crashed or partitioned holder's resource can be reclaimed.

Each successful acquire returns a fencing token that is a strictly increasing integer from a single monotonic per-resource counter, greater than any previous holder's token and never repeating or decreasing even across coordinator restarts.
A downstream store fences stale writers by tracking the highest accepted token and rejecting any protected operation carrying a token below that high-water mark.
A renewal extends an existing still-valid lease and keeps the same fencing token because the holder has not changed.
A renewal is honored only from the current holder while the lease is still valid, and is rejected once the lease has expired.
Expiry is decided solely by the coordinator's clock, which is the single authority on lease validity.
The lease duration promised to a client is the nominal duration reduced by a safety margin at least as large as the maximum assumed clock skew.

The client's validity view must be conservative: a client must consider its lease expired strictly before the coordinator does, never after, so it is never valid to the client while the coordinator already treats it as free.
The client interface is three operations — acquire(resource, client, ttl), renew(resource, client, token, ttl), and release(resource, client, token).
release frees the resource immediately and is honored only from the current holder presenting the current token, so a stale holder cannot release a re-granted lease.
Every operation whose preconditions do not hold is explicitly rejected rather than silently coerced.
